scenarios.title: SIGI Technologies AWS Full-Spectrum Evidence Lab
scenarios.risk_intent: Create a tagged, production-shaped AWS estate with intentionally mixed security posture across network, data, monitoring, compute, governance, secrets, containers, and IoT evidence domains.

expected_findings.reason: Public SSH, RDP, database, and broad ingress rules are present.
Security groups include broadly permissive ingress.
An empty S3 bucket is publicly readable and the public RDS instance is unencrypted.
CloudTrail exists but has no CloudWatch Logs integration, so retention evidence is absent.
The EC2 workload permits IMDSv1, is unmanaged by SSM, and has no AWS Backup coverage.
No AWS Config recorder, budget alert, or organization SCP coverage is created.
AWS IoT devices use an overbroad wildcard policy without Defender security profiles or private endpoints.

safety_notes: The EC2 instance has no key pair, credentials, application data, or IAM role.
The public S3 bucket remains empty and the RDS database contains no customer data.
All resources are tagged and managed by one CloudFormation stack.
The stack is intended for short-lived testing and carries a two-day deletion tag.

scenarios.title: AWS Public Exposure Evidence Lab
scenarios.risk_intent: Create controlled AWS control-plane evidence for public administrative ingress and public empty-object-storage exposure without launching EC2 workloads.

expected_findings.reason: Security group allows SSH and RDP from 0.0.0.0/0.
Empty lab S3 bucket has public-access blocks disabled and an allow-public-read bucket policy.
The lab does not create AWS Budgets or organization policy coverage.

safety_notes: The public S3 bucket is intended to remain empty.
The stack is tagged and can be deleted with the cleanup action.

scenarios.title: AWS Clean Baseline Evidence Lab
scenarios.risk_intent: Create a small tagged AWS baseline with private-only network defaults and a private encrypted S3 bucket.

expected_findings.reason: The lab does not create AWS Budgets or organization policy coverage.

safety_notes: The S3 bucket blocks public access and uses server-side encryption.
The stack is tagged and can be deleted with the cleanup action.
